proposals.title: Proposal to Adjust Annual Inflation Rate from 6% to 5% to Strengthen Long-Term Sustainability
proposals.summary:
This proposal suggests reducing the annual inflation rate of the Shido Network from 6% to 5%.

The primary objective is to enhance long-term economic sustainability while maintaining a balanced incentive structure for validators and delegators. A lower inflation rate will help reduce constant sell pressure caused by newly emitted tokens, improve scarcity, and support healthier price dynamics.

Rationale:
- Reduce ongoing sell pressure from inflation rewards
- Improve token scarcity and perceived value
- Strengthen long-term sustainability of the network economy
- Maintain competitive and fair staking incentives
- Align emission model with mature and stable blockchain ecosystems

Impact:
Lowering inflation to 5% is expected to create a more stable and predictable token economy, benefiting long-term holders, validators, and the broader ecosystem.

Risks:
- Slight reduction in short-term staking rewards
- Potential need for future adjustments based on network growth and fee dynamics

However, this adjustment is considered a balanced approach between sustainability and incentives.

proposals.title: Community Pool Spend: Boost WSHIDO Liquidity on Shido DEX (DWS & KENSEI)
proposals.summary:
This proposal requests a SHIDO community pool allocation to strengthen liquidity for two key Shido DEX pairs: DWS/WSHIDO and KENSEI/WSHIDO.

Why this matters:
- Higher TVL and deeper liquidity on Shido DEX
- Better market depth, lower slippage, and improved price stability
- Stronger long-term positioning of WSHIDO as the ecosystem’s primary settlement/liquidity asset

About DOGWIFSUIT (DWS):
- Utility-driven meme token backed by the BubbleSwap ecosystem and MavNode Labs
- Fully integrated into WenMint: paying minting fees in DWS reduces costs
- All DWS used for fees is permanently burned, creating continuous deflation driven by real on-chain usage
- Deep DWS/WSHIDO liquidity is essential infrastructure for smooth usage and efficient pricing

About KENSEI:
- Established Shido ecosystem project with an active user base and growing on-chain presence
- Expanding KENSEI/WSHIDO liquidity improves capital efficiency and helps reduce volatility across Shido DEX markets

Use of allocated funds:
1. Primary: Add and deepen liquidity for DWS/WSHIDO and KENSEI/WSHIDO to directly increase Shido DEX TVL.
2. Secondary: Enable transparent, controlled buyback mechanisms when needed, funded by ecosystem revenue (not speculative intervention).

Community pool liquidity provisioning is a common Cosmos-aligned approach to fund foundational on-chain infrastructure that increases activity and fee generation. This proposal deploys funds into productive, usage-backed liquidity rather than short-term incentives, hoping that more proposals of this kind will happen again in the future for trusted projects on Shido. The funds, a total of fourty million SHIDO, will be splitted in two, which is twenty million SHIDO for each project. 

Submitted by MavNode Labs 🧪.

proposals.title: Fix Missing Block Hash in EVM Event Logs
proposals.summary: This proposal applies a patch to fix an issue at the chain level where the EVM module was emitting event logs with an incorrect blockHash value (0x00000000…). Due to the missing block hash, event logs generated from smart contract transactions could not be properly decoded by explorers, subgraph indexers, and DEX infrastructure. These systems follow a standard process of verifying logs by first validating the transaction hash and block hash to confirm block existence before processing events. Because the block hash was invalid, log decoding and indexing failed. This upgrade updates the EVM module to correctly include the actual block hash in the event logs JSON, restoring standard EVM-compatible behavior. We recommend voting YES to approve this proposal and apply the fix on mainnet. Disclosure: This proposal has been submitted by the Shido Core Foundation. The upgrade guide is available here: https://github.com/ShidoGlobal/shido-upgrade-v3.3.1. The blockchain upgrade will take place at block height 27,750,000.

proposals.title: Shido Network V2 – Tera Mainnet Upgrade
proposals.summary: This official proposal seeks approval to upgrade the Shido Network mainnet through the implementation of the V2 Tera Upgrade. This upgrade introduces significant enhancements and optimizations to Shido’s core infrastructure, substantially improving network performance, throughput, and security. Upon approval, users and developers will benefit from a more efficient and reliable network experience when interacting with and building on the Shido Network blockchain.As part of this initiative, the Shido Core Foundation and Shido Network DevOps proposes measures to strengthen liquidity around the native token. To support expanded market reach and long-term growth, a calculated 25% increase in the non-circulating Shido supply is proposed. This adjustment is essential to enable the Shido Core Foundation to execute the 2026 token roadmap, which includes new decentralized exchange (DEX) listings, increased liquidity on the Shido DEX, additional centralized exchange listings, and deeper engagement with venture capital partners.It is important to note that this adjustment affects only non-circulating supply and is implemented as part of the V2 Tera Upgrade. The allocation will be verifiable on-chain within the Shido supply account and has been carefully structured to ensure a responsible, measured approach. This design supports Shido’s ability to achieve critical strategic objectives aimed at expanding the reach and market capitalization of the native Shido token.If this proposal is approved, the Shido Network blockchain will halt at a designated block height and resume operations using the upgraded Shido Network application binary.Additional technical details regarding this release are available in the official Shido GitHub repository.Disclosure: This proposal has been submitted by the Shido Core Foundation. The upgrade guide is available here: https://github.com/ShidoGlobal/shidochain-tera-upgrade.git. The blockchain upgrade will take place at block height 27,200,000.

proposals.title: Community Pool Funds Allocation – Burn or Continue Accumulation
proposals.summary:
This proposal invites the community to decide on the future of the community pool’s accumulated funds. The community must choose between two main actions:
 1. Burn all of the current community pool balance.
 2. Continue accumulating funds for future use cases and community-driven initiatives.

The outcome of this vote will shape how our network and stakeholders manage and utilize the community pool, reflecting our collective priorities regarding Shido supply and ongoing project funding.

CONTEXT AND RATIONALE
 1. What Is the Community Pool?
The community pool is a set of funds (usually denominated in the network’s native coin) allocated for network-related initiatives such as ecosystem grants, developer incentives, marketing activities, and security enhancements.
 2. Why Burn?
• Token Supply Control: Burning native coin can reduce inflationary pressure, potentially supporting coin value and demonstrating a commitment to supply management.
• Investor Confidence: Some community members believe that reducing the circulating supply may increase market confidence and long-term stability.

 3. Why Continue Accumulating?
• Future Funding: Maintaining or increasing funds in the pool preserves the flexibility to support new proposals, community grants, and bounties.
• Buffer for Emergencies: A sizeable pool can act as a contingency fund for unexpected events such as urgent upgrades or security incidents.
• Long-Term Vision: Sustained accumulation can be leveraged for strategic partnerships, user growth initiatives, or broader adoption campaigns.

PROPOSAL DETAILS

Option A: Burn the Community Pool
• Action: Burn all amount of the Shido in the community pool.
• Mechanics: Upon approval, the community pool Shido would be transferred to a burn address and removed from circulation.

Option B: Continue Accumulating Community Funds
• Action: Retain the current balance and allow the pool to keep growing under existing parameters (for instance, via staking rewards or transaction fees).
• Mechanics: No tokens would be destroyed. Funds remain available for future governance proposals, special initiatives, or emergency use.

VOTING OPTIONS
• Yes – Support burning the specified amount of the community pool.
• No – Oppose burning; continue with the current accumulation model.
• Abstain – No preference for either option; not counted in favor or against.
• NoWithVeto – Reject the proposal entirely if it is believed to be fundamentally flawed.

IMPLEMENTATION AND TIMELINE
 1. Proposal Submission: This proposal is open for discussion during the designated period (48 hours).
 2. Voting Period: After the discussion phase, on-chain voting will begin and last for the official duration (24 hours).
 3. Execution:
• If Option A (burn) receives a majority (with quorum met), tokens will be burned shortly after voting concludes.
• If Option B (accumulation) is chosen, no immediate action is required, and the community pool remains intact.

CONCLUSION
This proposal is intended to empower the community in setting the economic course of the network. Deciding whether to burn existing funds or continue to accumulate them will guide our approach to both short-term market dynamics and long-term growth. All Shido holders are encouraged to vote based on what they believe best serves the network’s vision and sustainability.

proposals.title: Software Upgrade v2.0.0
proposals.summary: We are conducting a significant software upgrade on the Shido network, with a primary focus on updating several core pckages, especially the ibc-go package from version 7.3.0 to 7.4.0. This update is crucial in addressing known security vulnerabilities within the Inter-Blockchain Communication (IBC) protocol, ensuring the continued safety and integrity of cross-chain transactions witin the Shido ecosystem. In addition to the ibc-go upgrade, we are updating several other core packages to their latest versions to improve overall performance and stability of the network. Furthermore, we have implemented the recommendations from the recent Zokyo blockchain protocols audit, addressing key findings to enhance the network's overall security. If the proposal passes, the software upgrade is planned to take place at block height 4,303,000. All node operators and validators must upgrade their binaries to the latest version to ensure compatibility and continued participation in the network. Detailed instructions for the upgrade process can be found in the following guide: https://github.com/ShidoGlobal/shidoupgrade_v2.0.0 This upgrade is essential for maintaining the security and efficiency of the Shido network, ensuring it remains robust against emerging threats and capable of supporting the evolving needs of the ecosystem.

proposals.title: Reduction of signed blocks window to 100000
proposals.summary: 1. Increasing Validator Accountability: Reducing the Signed Blocks Window makes the system more sensitive to validator downtime. This means that validators will need to pay closer attention to their participation in the validation process, as even short downtimes could lead to slashing or removal from the active set. Faster detection of inactive validators. If a validator stops signing blocks, the network detects this issue more quickly and takes appropriate action. 2. Reducing Network Latency Risk: If the signed blocks window is too large, the network might keep inactive validators in the active set for a longer time. This can increase block processing times or even cause delays if multiple validators go offline simultaneously. Reducing this parameter can help avoid these issues by quickly excluding inactive validators, ensuring more stable network performance. 3. Improving Decentralization: If the parameter is too large, large validators might sometimes 'miss' blocks, knowing they won't be penalized due to the long signed blocks window. Reducing this window forces all validators, regardless of their size, to actively participate in signing each block. This can promote a more even distribution of responsibility among validators and improve decentralization.

proposals.title: Validator Incentive Program (VIP) for Shido Network
proposals.summary:
Executive Summary:
The Validator Incentive Program (VIP) aims to attract and retain high-quality validators by rewarding those who demonstrate excellent performance, high uptime, and active participation in network decisions. This program seeks to enhance the security and stability of the Shido Network by incentivizing validators to maintain optimal performance and engagement.

Objectives:
1. Increase validator participation and improve network security.
2. Encourage validators to maintain high performance and uptime.
3. Reward active participation in network governance and decision-making.

Program Components:

- Performance-Based Rewards:
 - Uptime Rewards: Additional rewards for validators who achieve high uptime (e.g., above 99%).
 - Performance Bonuses: Extra incentives for validators with consistently high performance metrics.

- Participation Incentives:
 - Governance Participation Rewards: Bonuses for validators who actively participate in governance voting and decision-making processes.
 - Testnet Participation Rewards: Incentives for validators who contribute to testnet activities and help test new features and updates.

- Referral Bonuses:
 - Validator Referral Program: Rewards for existing validators who refer new, high-quality validators to the Shido Network.

Implementation Plan:

1. Define Metrics and Criteria:
 - Establish clear performance and participation metrics to determine eligibility for rewards.
 - Set up a transparent system for tracking validator performance and participation.

2. Launch and Outreach:
 - Announce the VIP to the validator community and conduct outreach to attract new validators.
 - Provide clear guidelines on how validators can qualify for rewards.

3. Monitoring and Adjustment:
 - Regularly monitor the effectiveness of the VIP and gather feedback from validators.
 - Adjust reward structures and criteria as needed to ensure the program’s success.

Budget and Funding:
- Allocate funds from the Community Pool for performance-based rewards, participation incentives, and referral bonuses.
- Ensure ongoing monitoring and administration costs are covered.

Conclusion:
The Validator Incentive Program (VIP) is designed to boost validator engagement and performance on the Shido Network. By offering targeted rewards for uptime, performance, and participation, the VIP will help maintain a robust and secure network, driving long-term success and resilience.
